title: Vectors
summary: How do you draw, add and split quantities that have a direction?
cards.0.p: A scalar quantity is described by a number and a unit. A vector quantity is described by a number, a unit and a direction. In this topic you will learn to draw vectors, add them and split them into components.
cards.0.key: Speed is a scalar, and velocity is a vector. "60 km/h" is a speed, while "60 km/h north" is a velocity.
cards.0.once.soru: Which one also needs a direction to describe it?
cards.0.once.secenekler.0.neden: Velocity also tells you which way something is going ("60 km/h north"). That makes it a vector.
cards.0.once.secenekler.1.neden: Mass has no direction. It is a scalar.
cards.0.once.secenekler.2.neden: Temperature has no direction. It is a scalar.
cards.1.p: We draw a vector as an arrow. The length of the arrow shows the magnitude, and its head shows the direction. The direction is given by the angle θ measured from the +x axis. Two vectors with the same length and direction are equal.
cards.1.key: The length of the arrow shows the magnitude, and the head shows the direction.
cards.2.p: First draw A, then put the tail of B at the head of A. The arrow drawn from the first tail to the last head is called the resultant (R = A + B). The order of adding does not change the result.
cards.2.key: The resultant is the arrow drawn from the first tail to the last head.
cards.3.p: Draw the two vectors from the same tail and complete the parallelogram. The diagonal from the shared tail to the opposite corner is the resultant. This method gives the same result as the head-to-tail method.
cards.3.key: The other diagonal of the parallelogram gives the difference A − B.
cards.3.once.soru: You draw two vectors from the same point and complete a parallelogram. Which one is the resultant?
cards.3.once.secenekler.0.yazi: The diagonal from the shared corner
cards.3.once.secenekler.0.neden: The diagonal from the shared tail to the opposite corner is the resultant. It gives the same result as adding head to tail.
cards.3.once.secenekler.1.neden: The perimeter is a sum of lengths. It is not a vector.
cards.3.once.secenekler.2.neden: The other diagonal gives the difference of the two vectors.
cards.4.p: When you multiply a vector by k, its length becomes |k| times as long. If k is positive the direction stays the same, and if k is negative it flips. For example, −A has the same length as A but points the opposite way.
cards.4.key: The length of kA is |k| times the length of A. If k is negative, the direction reverses.
cards.5.p: A − B really means A + (−B). So flip B, then add head to tail. For example, the change in velocity Δv = v<sub>final</sub> − v<sub>initial</sub> is found this way.
cards.5.once.soru: A ball moves right at 5 m/s, hits a wall and comes back left at 5 m/s. What is the magnitude of its change in velocity?
cards.5.once.secenekler.0.neden: Δv = v_final − v_initial = (−5) − (+5) = −10. Its magnitude is 10 m/s and it points left. Subtracting means adding the opposite.
cards.5.once.secenekler.1.neden: The speed stayed the same, but the direction changed. So the velocity vector changed.
cards.5.once.secenekler.2.neden: The velocity went from 5 to the right to 5 to the left. The difference is 10.
cards.6.h: Sin, cos and tan in a right triangle
cards.6.p: In a right triangle, sinθ is the ratio of the opposite side to the hypotenuse, and cosθ is the ratio of the adjacent side to the hypotenuse. tanθ is the ratio of the opposite side to the adjacent side. In a 3-4-5 triangle, the side opposite 37° is 3 and the side opposite 53° is 4.
cards.6.once.soru: A right triangle has legs of 3 and 4 units. How many units long is its longest side?
cards.6.once.secenekler.1.neden: You cannot simply add the sides. You need the Pythagorean theorem.
cards.7.p: You can split a slanted vector into two parts. They are found with V<sub>x</sub> = V·cosθ and V<sub>y</sub> = V·sinθ. If V = 10 and θ = 37°, then V<sub>x</sub> = 8 and V<sub>y</sub> = 6.
cards.7.key: The components are Vx = V·cosθ and Vy = V·sinθ. Here θ is the angle measured from the +x axis.
cards.8.p: If you know the components, the Pythagorean theorem is enough: V = √(V<sub>x</sub>² + V<sub>y</sub>²). The direction comes from tanθ = V<sub>y</sub> / V<sub>x</sub>. Check the signs of the components too.
cards.9.p: We can write a vector by its components. (3, 2) means 3 units right and 2 units up. (−2, 3) means 2 units left and 3 units up. With unit vectors it is written V = V<sub>x</sub>î + V<sub>y</sub>ĵ.
cards.9.key: The vector (3, 2) is also written 3î + 2ĵ. Adding by components is the most reliable way.
cards.9.once.soru: Which way does the vector (−2, 3) point?
cards.9.once.secenekler.0.neden: Negative x means left, and positive y means up.
cards.9.once.secenekler.1.neden: It goes left because x is negative and up because y is positive.
cards.9.once.secenekler.2.neden: The x component is negative. So the vector goes left, not right.
cards.10.p: The most reliable way to add vectors is to split them into components and add the x's and the y's separately. For example, if A = (4, 3) and B = (2, −3), then R = (6, 0).
cards.10.once.soru: A = (4, 3) and B = (2, −3). What is A + B?
cards.10.once.secenekler.0.neden: The x's add up to 4 + 2 = 6, and the y's add up to 3 + (−3) = 0.
cards.10.once.secenekler.1.neden: That result is A − B. To add, you add the x's and add the y's.
cards.11.h: When the angle between them is α
cards.11.p: If the angle between two vectors is α, then R² = A² + B² + 2AB·cosα. For α = 90° this turns into the Pythagorean theorem. If the angle is 0°, R = A + B, and if it is 180°, R = |A − B|.
cards.11.key: The larger the angle, the smaller the resultant. At 0° the resultant is A + B, and at 180° it is |A − B|.
cards.12.p: If the resultant of the forces is zero, the object is in equilibrium. Three forces in equilibrium form a closed triangle when added head to tail. By Lami's theorem, F₁ / sinα₁ = F₂ / sinα₂ = F₃ / sinα₃.
cards.12.svg#0: F₁ / sinα₁ = F₂ / sinα₂ = F₃ / sinα₃
cards.12.key: In Lami's theorem, α is the angle between the other two forces.
cards.12.once.soru: A sign hangs from two ropes and does not move. What is the resultant of the forces acting on the sign?
cards.12.once.secenekler.0.neden: An object at rest is in equilibrium. The resultant of the forces is zero.
cards.12.once.secenekler.1.neden: The forces in the ropes balance the weight, so the total is zero.
cards.12.once.secenekler.2.yazi: The sum of the rope forces
cards.12.once.secenekler.2.neden: The rope forces balance the weight, and the resultant is zero.
cards.13.p:
• A scalar has only a magnitude. A vector has a magnitude and a direction.
• Vectors are added head to tail or with the parallelogram method. A − B means A + (−B).
• The components are Vx = V·cosθ and Vy = V·sinθ.
• The magnitude is √(Vx² + Vy²).
quiz.0.q: The vectors A = (3, 5) and B = (1, −2) are given. What is the magnitude of the resultant A + B, in units?
quiz.0.e: Add the components separately: R = (3 + 1, 5 − 2) = (4, 3). Its magnitude is √(4² + 3²) = √25 = 5.
quiz.1.q: A 20 N force makes a 37° angle with the +x axis. What is the x component of the force, in N?
quiz.1.e: The horizontal component is F<sub>x</sub> = F·cos37° = 20 · 0.8 = 16 N. The vertical component is F<sub>y</sub> = 20 · 0.6 = 12 N.
quiz.2.q: Two equal vectors each have magnitude A. Match the angle between them with the magnitude of the resultant.
quiz.2.e: R² = A² + A² + 2A²·cosα. At 0° R = 2A, at 60° it is A√3, at 90° it is A√2, and at 120° it is A. At 180° the vectors point in opposite directions and R = 0.
quiz.3.q: Which of these CANNOT be the resultant of two forces of 3 N and 5 N?
quiz.3.e: The resultant must lie between |5 − 3| = 2 N and 5 + 3 = 8 N. So 9 N is not possible.
quiz.3.y.0: 2 N is the smallest resultant, reached when the forces point in opposite directions. So it is possible.
quiz.3.y.1: 5 N lies between 2 N and 8 N, so it can be reached with a suitable angle.
quiz.3.y.2: 8 N is the largest resultant, reached when the forces point the same way. So it is possible.
A:ozet: Try first, learn the name after. Draw a vector, rotate and add, then split it into components.
A:adimlar.0.metin: θ is the angle the arrow makes with the +x axis (pointing right). Draw the vector with length 3 units and θ = 135°.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.tamam: Since 135° = 90° + 45°, the arrow points up and to the left.
A:adimlar.1.metin: A is 3 units long and B is 4 units long. Rotate B and make the resultant exactly 5 units.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.tamam: When A and B are perpendicular they form a right triangle, and R = √(3² + 4²) = 5. The magnitude of the resultant depends on the angle between the vectors. Adding the numbers is not enough.
A:adimlar.2.baslik: How big can the resultant be?
A:adimlar.2.metin: Turn B from 0° to 180° and watch how the resultant changes.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.soru: In what range does the resultant of two vectors of 3 and 4 units stay?
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: For the resultant to be zero, the vectors would need equal lengths. Set B to 180° and look.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: It is largest in the same direction (3 + 4 = 7) and smallest in opposite directions (4 − 3 = 1). The resultant always lies between |A − B| and A + B.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: Set B to 0°. The resultant becomes 7, which is more than 4.
A:adimlar.3.metin: Make a vector twice as long as A but pointing the opposite way.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.tamam: This vector is −2A. It is twice as long and points the opposite way.
A:adimlar.4.metin: V is 10 units long. Change the angle and make the vertical component 5.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.tamam: Since sin30° = 0.5, V<sub>y</sub> = 10 × 0.5 = 5. The horizontal component is V<sub>x</sub> = 10 × cos30° ≈ 8.66.
A:adimlar.5.metin: You walked 3 steps east. How many steps north must you walk to be exactly 5 steps from where you started?
A:adimlar.5.gorev.tamam: √(3² + 4²) = 5. You walked 7 steps in total, but your displacement is 5 steps. The total length of your path (the distance) is a scalar, while displacement is a vector.
A:kapanis.0: A scalar quantity is given by a number and a unit (mass, temperature, time). A vector quantity also needs a direction (force, velocity, displacement).
A:kapanis.1: For vectors added head to tail, the resultant is the arrow from the first tail to the last head. The resultant always lies between |A − B| and A + B.
A:kapanis.2: The length of kA is |k| times the length of A, and if k is negative the direction is reversed. A − B means A + (−B).
A:kapanis.3: The components are Vx = V·cosθ and Vy = V·sinθ. The magnitude is V = √(Vx² + Vy²).
